approved: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Legislation Amendment (Safety and Other Measures) Bill 2024
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill aims to improve safety for workers on offshore oil and gas facilities by updating the existing legal framework.
It would change the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006 to adopt recommendations from a government safety review and make other adjustments.

New rules would require vessel operators to tell the regulator when they start or stop working as a facility, and the changes would take effect before the current safety regulations expire on 1 April 2026.
Align health and safety representative training with the Work Health and Safety Act 2011.
Let health and safety representatives ask to review safety management documents.
Let health and safety representatives serve on health and safety committees.
Broaden the definition of health to cover physical and mental aspects.
Add new duties for titleholders when a different company runs the facility.
Set up a scheme requiring operators to notify the regulator when starting or ending work as a facility.
Offshore oil and gas workers, facility operators, titleholders, and the regulator NOPSEMA.

In other words, they voted to agree with the main idea of the bill and so it can now be discussed in detail. ### What does this bill do? According to the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd2324a/24bd056) (which is a document prepared by the parliamentary library): * *The Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Legislation Amendment (Safety and Other Measures) Bill 2024 seeks to amend the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006 (OPGGS Act) to improve safety outcomes for Australia’s offshore resources sector workforce.* * *The Bill makes a range of amendments to the OPGGS Act, including to Schedule 3 which relates to occupational health and safety.* * *The Bill implements some recommendations of Offshore Oil and Gas Safety Review which began in 2018. However, the majority of the recommendations will be implemented through the remake of the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Safety) Regulations 2009, which are due to sunset on 1 April 2026. A draft of proposed regulations is not yet available.* * *The Bill also proposes to introduce a new section that would preserve approvals made under NOPSEMA’s Endorsed Program authorised by the strategic assessment under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act).
